_comment: Which recordings the app ships. One speaker per lesson, so a lesson has a
consistent voice while the course as a whole stays multi-speaker — learners
generalise better from varied talkers than from one.
Speaker names are as Commons writes them: the person first, the account that
uploaded the recording in brackets. The dataset zips reverse the two; either
"words": "*" takes everything that speaker recorded; "vocab" takes every
word data.js teaches that anyone recorded. Name words explicitly to curate a
subset. Run `python3 tools/build_audio.py --report` to see who recorded what.

lessons.title: Existing vocabulary
_note: Not a lesson — recordings for the vocabulary the app taught before the
corpus arrived. "*" pools every speaker: these words are scattered
across contributors, and for a word the learner meets inside an older
category, having a native recording matters more than matching a voice.
"vocab" rather than a hand-copied list because the app no longer speaks
anything it has no recording for. A word that is in the curriculum and in
the corpus but not in this file is simply silent, and a list maintained by
